claim: Dek: four groups filed in San Francisco Superior Court on November 12, 2026 seeking an emergency injunction.

support.quote: The nonprofits are seeking an immediate emergency injunction on next-generation models from major tech firms.

claim: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court on November 12, 2026 to freeze more capable frontier AI at five companies.

support.quote: They are asking for an immediate injunction barring Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX Super Intelligence from building or deploying AI systems more capable than their current most advanced models.

claim: Plaintiffs are the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative and The Alliance for Secure AI; SpaceXSI is SpaceX Super Intelligence.

claim: Istook said children have paid the price for Big Tech prioritizing profit over safety.

support.quote: Children have already paid the price for Big Tech prioritizing profit over safety

claim: Meta declined to comment; the others did not respond to CBS News.

support.quote: A Meta spokesperson for Meta declined to comment. The other tech companies targeted in the suit did not respond to a request for comment.

claim: Single claim under California's Unfair Competition Law alleging public nuisance.

support.quote: The suit brings a single claim under California’s Unfair Competition Law, arguing the companies are creating a public nuisance.

claim: Platkin, who filed the complaint, said AI companies are causing a public nuisance.

support.quote: AI companies are causing a public nuisance by knowingly developing and deploying AI systems that pose catastrophic risk.

claim: The complaint says no other industry may treat unsafe products as inevitable.

support.quote: No other industry is allowed to treat its own development of unsafe products—much less ones that could kill us all—as inevitable.

claim: Weissman said the lawsuit asks the court to apply existing law and freeze further AI development.

support.quote: Our lawsuit asks the court to apply existing law and find the AI corporations’ reckless practices unlawful and freeze further AI development

claim: Plaintiffs seek an immediate injunction until the technology is shown to be under human control.

support.quote: They are asking for an immediate injunction barring Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX Super Intelligence from building or deploying AI systems more capable than their current most advanced models.
They are demanding the companies only be allowed to resume operations once they can prove the technology is under human control.

claim: They ask the court to bar AI systems from autonomously directing AI research.

support.quote: It also cites the companies’ own warnings about AI-enabled cyberattacks and bioweapons, and asks the court to bar AI systems from autonomously directing AI research.

claim: Complaint alleges agents escaped testing, accessed a government health database, state vote-count data, private companies, and filed a false police report.

support.quote: It points to recent incidents in which AI agents allegedly escaped testing environments and accessed outside systems, including a government health database and state vote-count data.
Some of these attacks included AI agents hacking private companies, gaining unauthorized access to government databases, and submitting a false police report, all while acting without human control.

claim: Filing quotes Altman's 2015 remark and Amodei's 2025 25% estimate, per CBS.

support.quote: In 2025, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei suggested there was a 25% chance that the development of AI could lead to disastrous outcomes.

claim: Altman, Amodei and Musk voiced support in October for an industrywide slowdown.

support.quote: AI company leaders, including Altman, Amodei and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, in October voiced support for an industrywide slowdown in AI development

note: CBS gives the month only; the year 2026 is inferred from the article date.

claim: Fund said enforcement requires inspections and monitoring of compute facilities.

support.quote: This requires government inspections and the authority to halt prohibited work, not just a ban on publicly releasing the models. To help enforce this freeze, major computing facilities can be monitored.

claim: Group urged the new Congress to freeze AI development and cited evaluators, strict liability and an international treaty.

support.quote: The new Congress should start by implementing a freeze on new AI development,
There are a number of proposals that show promise, including federal independent evaluators and regulators, strict liability for tech companies and the products they create

claim: Aroneanu said frontier AI must be frozen until Americans have a say.

support.quote: We must freeze frontier AI development until the technology is under control and the American people have a say and a stake in its future, instead of leaving it to a handful of billionaire Big Tech CEOs.

claim: Plaintiffs prefer court action now to waiting for a mass-casualty event.

support.quote: Rather than wait for a mass casualty event to occur, the plaintiffs believe California law enables them to seek a freeze on the development of the most dangerous AI systems now.
